findings.failure_mode: Missing or unreadable file at `path` aborts the entire program with a panic instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle gracefully
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use .map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e))

findings.failure_mode: Non-numeric or out-of-range value in the CSV causes a panic at runtime instead of returning a typed ParseError the caller can recover from
findings.fix: Use .map_err(|e| LoadError::Parse(e)) and return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>

findings.problem: as u16 cast after parse — lossy conversion from u32 to u16
findings.failure_mode: Values in range 65536..=4294967295 silently truncate to u16 range, producing incorrect domain values without any error or bounds check
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| LoadError::Overflow) or parse directly as u16 with .parse::<u16>().map_err(...)

findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV line with fewer than 2 fields causes a panic at runtime via index out of bounds

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) — stdout I/O inside data-loading logic
findings.failure_mode: Logging side effect leaks into the data pipeline, contaminating pure computation with shell-side I/O, making the function non-reproducible, non-testable, and violating the Data/Calculations/Actions separation
findings.fix: Remove println! entirely from the pipeline; move any observability to the shell layer outside load_shards

findings.problem: load_shards fuses file I/O, allocation, parsing, logging, println!, domain construction, and type conversion into a single function
findings.failure_mode: Cannot test parsing logic in isolation; cannot reuse the domain type without file access; shell responsibilities leak into the core making the entire function fragile and untestable
findings.fix: Split into: (1) a pure parse_record(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> for calculations, (2) a shell-level load_shards that handles fs::read_to_string, calls parse_record per line, and collects results

findings.problem: load_shards takes &str path (file system) instead of accepting already-read data, fusing I/O with parsing and domain construction
findings.failure_mode: The function cannot be unit-tested for parsing correctness without real files on disk; hidden file I/O makes the function's behavior depend on external state rather than its inputs
findings.fix: Make load_shards accept &[String] or &str lines and return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>; the shell layer calls fs::read_to_string and passes lines to the pure parser

findings.problem: Record uses raw String for name and raw u16 for value — no parse boundary, no domain validation, no newtype
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct Record with empty names, invalid UTF-8, or values outside domain meaning; illegal states are fully representable at the type level
findings.fix: Use a Name newtype with a smart constructor that validates non-empty and bounded length; validate value range in the parser; Record should only accept validated types

findings.problem: No input size cap, no try_reserve, no max record limit — unbounded Vec allocation from file contents
findings.failure_mode: A very large file allocates unbounded memory, potentially causing OOM; no domain cap prevents resource exhaustion attacks
findings.fix: Add a trusted max_records cap; validate input size before allocation; use Vec::new() + try_reserve(max_records).map_err(...) instead of implicit Vec::with_capacity or unbounded collect

findings.problem: load_shards returns Vec<Record> — all fallible operations (I/O, parse, indexing, cast) are hidden behind unwrap, discarding error information
findings.failure_mode: Callers have no way to distinguish between file-not-found, malformed data, out-of-range values, or index errors; error handling is impossible at the call site
findings.fix: Define a LoadError enum (Io, Parse, Invalid, Overflow) and return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for load_shards performance characteristics
findings.failure_mode: Cannot verify that the function meets latency or throughput targets; unbounded allocation and per-line Vec/String allocation may dominate runtime for large inputs
findings.fix: Add a criterion or divan benchmark measuring load_shards against realistic shard files; profile allocation patterns and compare against a try_reserve + typed-error version
